info.title: Strategy Service API
info.description:
REST API for asynchronous strategy backtests, live strategy runs, and strategy discovery.

All endpoints except `/healthz` require:
- `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- `tenant-id: <id>` — DORA tenant identifier required on every authed request and forwarded on outbound DORA calls. See the TenantID parameter.

---

Bond-trading-strategy agent: HTTP surface for prompt handling, session
state, and strategy capture. Authentication is the user-level Dora
`ApiKey` token (not the LLM provider key — that lives in
`/v1/provider-config`). The agent's HTTP layer only validates the
inbound `Authorization` header format; it does not know the upstream
Dora API's auth conventions, and per the dora-agent middleware only
accepts the literal `ApiKey <token>` prefix (see security scheme below).

get.summary: Open a WebSocket connection for real-time lifecycle notifications
get.description: Upgrades the HTTP connection to a WebSocket. The server authenticates using the standard Authorization header (ApiKey <key> or Bearer <token>), resolves the DORA user, and streams JSON-encoded Event objects as text frames. Clients that cannot set request headers may alternatively pass `x-api-key` as a query parameter; the header takes precedence when both are present. Optional query params: Last-Event-ID (UUIDv7) replays events from the log; types (comma-separated) filters by EventType. Heartbeat is WS-level ping/pong every 30s.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Replay events with id > Last-Event-ID (UUIDv7). Capped at 1000 events or 24h, whichever is smaller.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated whitelist of EventType values. Default: all.

parameters.name: x-api-key
parameters.description: Alternative to the Authorization header for clients that cannot set request headers on the WebSocket handshake. Ignored when the Authorization header is present.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Inclusive lower bound on created_at. Malformed values are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Inclusive upper bound on created_at. Malformed values are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 50, silently clamped to [1, 200].

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation token returned by a previous call. Malformed values are rejected with 400.

get.summary: List the trading decisions recorded for a live strategy run, newest first
get.description: Returns the strategy_decisions rows for a single run owned by the authenticated user. Backtest runs are not represented in this table. The user is derived from the auth token, not the URL — wrong-user and not-found both produce 404. The cursor is opaque and versioned; do not parse it.

post.summary: Save or replace the user's provider config (LLM credentials + base_url).
post.description:
The api_key value is encrypted at rest with the AGENT_MASTER_KEY
envelope. base_url is optional; when set, it routes provider
traffic to a custom endpoint (OpenRouter, Together, on-prem proxy).
For tests against a plain http:// httptest stub, set
`AGENT_ALLOW_HTTP_BASE_URL=1` on the binary's environment — the
handler relaxes the https:// check only when that flag is present.

400.description:
Invalid JSON, missing api_key/default_model, unsupported
provider, or non-https:// base_url without the bypass flag.

get.summary: List the user's configured providers.
get.description:
Returns the user's configured providers with the api_key masked
(`sk-...abcd` form). The KMS-backed decryption happens in the
providerconfig store; the handler just renders the masked form
as `api_key_masked`.

delete.summary: Delete the user's config for one provider.

404.description: Provider config not found for this user.

post.description:
Requires that the user has previously saved a provider config
for `provider`; otherwise the request fails with 409. The model
field is stored on the session and used as the default when the
subsequent message request omits it.

409.description:
Provider/model missing from body, or no saved provider config
for the given provider for this user.

get.summary: List the user's sessions, newest first.
Get a session and its messages.

post.summary: Post a user prompt and stream the assistant turn as Server-Sent Events.
post.description:
The handler validates the prompt, persists it as a
`role=user` message, runs the four-layer sanitisation pass
(HTTP filter → LLM classifier → system prompt → source pattern
scan), then drives the tool loop. Events are written to the SSE
stream as they happen. The assistant turn is persisted to the
`messages` table when the stream completes successfully; on
internal failure the runner still emits its accumulated text via
partial `delta` events and an `error` event.

SSE event names (the `event:` field):
  - `delta`: streaming assistant text (`{"text": "..."}`)
  - `tool_call`: tool invocation (`{"id","name","input"}`)
  - `refusal`: classifier returned off_topic (`{"reason": "..."}`)
  - `strategy_saved`: a verified strategy version was captured
    (`{"strategy_id","revision","module_name","summary"}`)
  - `done`: turn complete (`{"reason": "..."}`)
  - `error`: turn failed (`{"message": "..."}`)

Refusal events always precede `done`; error events may occur at
any point and do not have a corresponding `done`. `strategy_saved`
is emitted by the capture observer mid-turn and does not end the
stream; a `done` still follows.

503.description: Agent runtime unavailable (server started without one).

post.summary: Consume the session's stashed pending strategy capture.
post.description:
Idempotent: a second save with no pending capture returns 404.
The session must already exist (otherwise 404). Strategy-store
must be wired (otherwise 503).

200.description: Capture recorded as a strategy version.

404.description: Session not found, or no pending strategy.

get.summary: List the user's strategies.
Get a strategy by ID.
get.description:
Returns the strategy plus a best-effort head-version summary
(revision, created_at, module_name, summary). When the head
version can't be resolved the `head` object is present but all
its fields are empty strings.

get.summary: List versions for a strategy, newest first.
Get one version (with file contents).

post.summary: Roll the strategy head back to a prior revision.
post.description:
Revision is taken from the request body (not the URL). The
target revision must already exist for the strategy. After the
call, the strategy's `head_revision` points at `revision` and a
new audit row is written.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, missing revision, or revision not in the strategy's history.

post.summary: Set the kill switch for the strategy's user.
post.description: Halts every live strategy the authenticated user owns (Plan 4). The kill switch is per-user; the strategy id is path-scoped but one halt stops all of the user's running strategies.
Clears the per-user kill switch so the user's strategies may resume (Plan 4).
Clears the per-strategy restart budget so the orchestrator will restart the strategy on the next watcher tick (Plan 4). Returns 501 until the orchestrator is wired.

post.summary: Trigger a live deployment of a strategy version.
post.description:
Starts the recorded image for the version in live mode and
returns a deployment_id. Async — poll the status endpoints.

202.description: Deployment accepted and created; strategy is starting in live mode. Poll GET /v1/strategies/{id}/deployments/{deployment_id} for status.

get.summary: List deployments for a strategy.
Get a deployment's status.
Retrieve (later: stream) deployment logs.
get.description:
Placeholder. Slice D design will define the log contract —
likely SSE once the runtime supports log streaming. Returns 501
until then.

post.summary: Trigger a backtest of a strategy version.
post.description:
Runs the recorded image for the version in backtest mode
(historic replay + simulated fills) and returns a backtest_id.
Async — poll GET /v1/strategies/{id}/backtests/{backtest_id}.

get.summary: List backtest jobs for a strategy.
Get a backtest's status/result.

post.summary: Mint a fresh admin bearer token.
post.description:
Unauthenticated (the only such route). Generates a 32-byte
random token, stores its SHA-256 hash in process memory, and
returns the plaintext token exactly once in the response body.
The operator persists it to ~/.config/dora-agent/admin-token via
`agent-cli admin init`. Returns 409 when the server is already
initialized (either a prior /admin/init, or AGENT_ADMIN_TOKEN_HASH
set at startup for already-deployed servers).

409.description: Server already initialized (in-memory token or AGENT_ADMIN_TOKEN_HASH set).

post.summary: Rotate the server's Admin Dora API key.
post.description:
Seals the new plaintext key with envelope encryption
(internal/secrets) and upserts it into
server_dora_credentials (the id=0 sentinel). Requires the admin
bearer token. The old key is overwritten.

Sanity check. Returns `{"auth":"admin"}` when the bearer token
matches the stored hash; 401 otherwise.

doraApiKey.name: Authorization
doraApiKey.description:
User-level Dora ApiKey token. **The agent's middleware only
accepts the literal `ApiKey <token>` prefix**; the broader
OpenAPI convention for this header would be `Bearer <token>`.
The upstream Dora API may also accept Bearer (verify against
the dora-api skill if you need that compatibility); the agent
itself does not.

adminBearer.description:
Operator-only admin token (32 random bytes, base64url). The
server stores only its SHA-256 hash in process memory; the
plaintext is shown once in the `POST /admin/init` response
and then carried by the agent-cli as `Authorization: Bearer
<token>`. Lives on a separate loopback listener
(127.0.0.1:AGENT_ADMIN_ADDR, default :9090) — never the
public API port. `/admin/init` is the only unauthenticated
route; `/admin/rotate-key` and `/admin/whoami` require it.

TenantID.name: tenant-id
TenantID.description: DORA tenant identifier required on every authed request; forwarded to DORA on every outbound call.

Revision.name: revision
Revision.description: Revision identifier (a string the strategy store assigns).

PageLimit.name: limit
PageLimit.description:
Maximum items per page. EffectiveLimit caps the value at 100 and
defaults to 50 when omitted or zero.

PageCursor.name: cursor
PageCursor.description:
Opaque keyset cursor returned as `next_cursor` by the previous
page. Omit for the first page; pass the returned value to fetch
the next page.

DeploymentId.name: deployment_id
DeploymentId.description: Deployment job identifier (assigned by the server).

BacktestId.name: backtest_id
BacktestId.description: Backtest job identifier (assigned by the server).

NotImplemented.description: Strategy is known but not implemented for the requested operation

Conflict.description: A strategy is already active for this order book

Unauthorized.description: Missing or malformed Authorization header, or rejected by upstream.

StrategyStoreUnavailable.description: Strategy version store is not wired on the server.

AgentNotImplemented.description:
The route exists but the feature (slice D deployment or slice E
backtest orchestration) is not yet implemented. Returned as a
stable placeholder; slice D/E design will replace the body.

CopyTraderSummary.description: A single entry in the list-copy-traders response. The `id` is the DORA user id and matches the `followed_trader` field accepted by CopyTradingConfig. `user_name` is the DORA-registered handle surfaced for display in copy-trading run configuration UIs.

order_book_id.description: DORA order book UUID used to locate the traded asset and place orders.

initial_balance.description: Starting capital for backtests. Omitted for live runs — obtained from DORA positions.

BreakoutConfig.description: Volatility-compression / price-breakout strategy. Enters when short-window price volatility drops below a threshold of long-window volatility, then a close breaks above (or below) a k·ATR trigger band.

long_vol_window.description: Long-window price-volatility observation count. Must be greater than short_vol_window.

compression_threshold.description: ShortVol/LongVol ratio below which the strategy arms for a breakout.

atr_window.description: Rolling-mean window for ATR (mean absolute price diff).

breakout_atr_multiple.description: Number of ATR units above/below the most recent close that defines the breakout trigger band.

confirmation_bars.description: Number of consecutive closes beyond the trigger band required to fire.

stop_loss_atr.description: Stop-loss distance in ATR units. Mirrored in the live Run loop and the backtester.

take_profit_atr.description: Take-profit distance in ATR units from entry. Set to 0 to disable. Mirrored in the live Run loop and the backtester.

obv_window.description: Recent trades to include in windowed OBV (On-Balance Volume). 0 = no volume verification; > 0 verifies signals with the last N trades, sourced from the live trade stream (runs) or trades_history (backtests).

obv_trend_threshold.description: Absolute OBV threshold the breakout signal must clear when obv_window > 0. Direction-mapped.

min_long_vol_floor.description: Minimum LongVol required to trade. Suppresses entries on a completely flat baseline.

order_book_id.description: DORA order book UUID used to locate the traded asset and place orders.

initial_balance.description: Starting capital for backtests. Omitted for live runs — obtained from DORA positions.

MomentumConfig.description: Moving-average-crossover trend strategy with configurable signal source (price / ytm / spread) and entry-anchored ATR exits.

signal_source.description: Series the MA crossover runs on. `spread` requires `tenor`.

slow_window.description: Slow-MA tick window. Must be greater than fast_window.

stop_loss_atr.description: Stop-loss distance in ATR units. 0 disables.

take_profit_atr.description: Take-profit distance in ATR units. 0 disables.

min_order_size.description: Skip opening when the computed quantity is below this. 0 disables.

max_order_size.description: Clamp the order quantity down to this. 0 disables.

max_position_size.description: Maximum fraction of capital allocated per trade.

tenor.description: Benchmark Treasury tenor (e.g. 2Y, 5Y, 10Y). Required when signal_source is spread.

initial_balance.description: Starting capital. Must be greater than 0 for backtests; live runs may pass 0 to use the user's DORA USD balance.

followed_trader.description: DORA user id of the trader whose trades will be copied.

percentage_of_available.description: Fraction of available balance to allocate per copied trade. Must be in (0, 1].

leverage.description: Leverage multiplier applied to copied orders. Must be greater than 0.

min_order_size.description: Minimum order size; orders below this threshold are skipped. Defaults to 0.

max_order_size.description: Maximum order size; orders above this threshold are clipped. Must be >= min_order_size. Defaults to 0 (no cap).

disallowed_bonds.description: Bond UUIDs to exclude from copying. If absent or empty, all bonds are eligible.

initial_balance.description: Starting cash for backtests. Omit or set to 0 to use the package default (10000). Omitted for live runs — obtained from DORA positions.

error.description: Error message if the backtest failed

BacktestResultSummary.description: Flattened backtest result returned by GET /v1/backtests/{id}. Mirrors the Go BacktestResultSummary struct — contains result fields at top level alongside strategy type, status, and config, but omits id, dora_user_id, and timestamps.

error.description: Error message if the backtest failed

MomentumTradeRecord.description: Momentum trade row emitted by GET /v1/backtests/{id}/trades for momentum backtests.

fast_ma.description: Fast MA at the decision. Not persisted (no backing column); always empty on rows read back from this endpoint.

slow_ma.description: Slow MA at the decision. Not persisted (no backing column); always empty on rows read back from this endpoint.

entry_atr.description: ATR captured on the opening row; mirrored onto the matching exit row.

MomentumClosedTrade.description: Momentum closed-trade row emitted by GET /v1/backtests/{id}/closed-trades for momentum backtests.

pnl.description: Profit/loss in price terms: quantity x (exit_price - entry_price), signed by direction.

exit_reason.description: One of stop_loss, take_profit, reversal, strategy_exit.

BreakoutTradeRecord.description: Breakout trade row emitted by GET /v1/backtests/{id}/trades for breakout backtests.

compression_ratio.description: Short-window / long-window volatility ratio at the tick that armed the breakout (armed ratio on entry rows).

entry_atr.description: ATR captured on the opening row; mirrored onto the matching exit row.

BreakoutClosedTrade.description: Breakout closed-trade row emitted by GET /v1/backtests/{id}/closed-trades for breakout backtests.

pnl.description: Profit/loss in price terms: quantity x (exit_price - entry_price), signed by direction.

exit_reason.description: One of stop_loss, take_profit, reversal, strategy_exit.

entry_compression_ratio.description: Compression ratio at the entry tick (short/long window volatility).

exit_compression_ratio.description: Compression ratio at the exit tick.

Event.description: A single notification event delivered over the WebSocket. New event types (notably dora.*) may appear without a spec change — clients MUST tolerate unknown values of `type`.

id.description: UUIDv7. Monotonic; used as the Last-Event-ID replay cursor.

user_id.description: DORA user id the event belongs to.

timestamp.description: Event timestamp in RFC3339, always UTC.

NotificationLogEntry.description: Internal. Persisted copy of an Event used for Last-Event-ID replay. Not exposed via the REST API.

Decision.description: One trading decision recorded during a live strategy run. The row is the source of truth for the inputs that produced a single market order; clients should treat all fields as immutable audit data.

DecisionList.description: One page of trading decisions. next_cursor is omitted on the last page; clients should treat absent and empty string the same.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation token. Pass back as the cursor query parameter to fetch the next page. Clients MUST NOT parse this value.

allOf.description: Provider identifier. openai/anthropic for direct API access, openrouter for unified multi-provider access.

api_key.description: LLM provider secret. Encrypted at rest.

default_model.description: Default model. See CreateSessionRequest.model for the full list.

base_url.description:
Optional custom endpoint. Must be https:// unless the
`AGENT_ALLOW_HTTP_BASE_URL=1` bypass is set on the binary.

api_key_masked.description: Masked form of the api_key (the real implementation returns this).

allOf.description: LLM provider. Model names are provider-scoped (see model field).

Model name. Use a bare family name for provider=openai (e.g. gpt-5) or provider=anthropic (e.g. claude-opus-4); use a `provider/model` address for provider=openrouter (e.g. openai/gpt-5). For OpenRouter free-tier inference, append `:free` (e.g. `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`); see OpenRouterFreeModel for the curated list.

strategies.description:
Every strategy produced by this session, newest first. Lets
the chat UI surface "view code" for historically captured
strategies even when the SSE `strategy_saved` event was
missed (binary restart, event dropped, pre-wiring capture).

tool_calls.description:
Raw JSON payload for tool-role messages (json.RawMessage on
the wire — emitted as raw JSON, typically an array of
tool-call objects). Opaque; consumers should not
introspect its structure. Absent for user/assistant roles.

prompt.description: User prompt to send to the agent.

provider.description: Override the session's saved provider for this turn.

allOf.description: Override the session's saved model for this turn. Same form rules as CreateSessionRequest.model.

MessageStream.description:
Server-Sent Events stream. Each event is `event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n`.
The `name` is one of `delta`, `tool_call`, `refusal`, `strategy_saved`,
`done`, `error`. The `data` payload is the corresponding JSON object below.

MessageStreamStrategySaved.description:
Emitted mid-turn by the capture observer when a verified strategy
version is recorded. Does not end the stream; `done` still follows.

HeadSummary.description:
Best-effort summary of the strategy's head version. All fields
are empty strings when the head version can't be resolved.

StrategyLink.description:
Slim reference to a strategy produced by a session, used by
GET /v1/sessions/{id} so the chat UI can fetch source files via
GET /v1/strategies/{id}/versions/{revision}.

files.description: Map of relative path → file contents.

target.description: Strategy target. go-wasm strategies run as WASM plugins (Plan 4).

wasm_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the .wasm blob in the artifact store. Non-null iff target == go-wasm.

manifest_hash.description: Content-addressed reference to the manifest.json sidecar. Non-null iff target == go-wasm.

target.description: Strategy target. go-wasm strategies run as WASM plugins.

wasm_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the .wasm blob in the artifact store. Omitted until the version is built (target == go-wasm).

manifest_hash.description: Content-addressed reference to the manifest.json sidecar. Omitted until the version is built (target == go-wasm).

revision.description: Revision identifier to roll back to.

DeployRequest.description:
Live-deployment configuration for a strategy version. The
server starts the recorded image for the version in live mode
against the given order book and resolution.

order_book_id.description: Dora order book to trade against (e.g. "usdc-usdt").

params.description: Optional runtime parameters passed to the strategy (string key → string value).

warmup_candles.description: Preamble warmup window from the strategy manifest (resolution-spaced candles); persisted on the deployment row so resume/recover need not reload the manifest. 0 when omitted.

DeployResponse.description:
Returned on successful deployment creation. The deployment
starts asynchronously; poll
GET /v1/strategies/{id}/deployments/{deployment_id} for status.

status.description: Initial deployment status. A freshly created deployment is running.

revision.description: Strategy version revision this deployment runs.

instance_id.description: Runtime instance identifier. Omitted until the deployment has been scheduled onto a runtime.

order_book_id.description: Dora order book the deployment trades against.

started_at.description: When the deployment entered the running state. Null before it starts.

stopped_at.description: When the deployment was stopped or halted. Null while running.

stopped_reason.description: Human-readable reason the deployment stopped, if any.

restart_count.description: Number of times the deployment has been automatically restarted.

hotswapped_at.description: When the deployment was last hot-swapped to a new revision. Null if never hot-swapped.

hotswapped_from_rev.description: Revision the deployment ran before its last hot-swap. Null if never hot-swapped.

params.description: Runtime parameters the deployment was started with (string key → string value).

candle_count.description: Number of candles the deployment has processed.

created_at.description: When the deployment record was created.

updated_at.description: When the deployment record was last updated.

next_cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for the next page. Omitted when there are no more results.

order_book_id.description: Dora order book ID the strategy will trade on. The framework reads this from ORDER_BOOK_ID and uses it to fetch historic candles. Required; the LLM asks the user for it if not known.

warmup_candles.description: Preamble warmup window (resolution-spaced candles) fetched before the window start so OnPreamble sees history. 0 when omitted.

BacktestRequest.description: Backtest configuration for a strategy version: the time window, candle resolution, and the order book to trade on.

BacktestResponse.description:
Placeholder. Identifies the created backtest; clients poll
GET /v1/strategies/{id}/backtests/{backtest_id} for status/result.

Backtest.description:
Placeholder. A backtest job's status/result (id, revision,
state, results, ...). Slice E design will define the fields.

token.description:
Fresh admin bearer token (base64url 32 random bytes). Shown
only here; the server stores only its SHA-256 hash.

AdminInitResponse.description:
The plaintext admin token. The operator persists it to
~/.config/dora-agent/admin-token via `agent-cli admin init`.

key.description:
New Admin Dora API key (plaintext). Sealed with envelope
encryption before persistence.

AdminWhoamiResponse.description: Sanity-check reply confirming the bearer token authenticated.

Provider.description: Provider identifier. openai/anthropic for direct API access, openrouter for unified multi-provider access.

Model.description: Model name. For provider=openai, use the bare family name (e.g. gpt-5). For provider=anthropic, use the bare family name (e.g. claude-opus-4). For provider=openrouter, use the prefixed form `provider/model` (e.g. openai/gpt-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4). See the OpenAIModel, AnthropicModel, and OpenRouterModel components for the full per-provider lists.

OpenAIModel.description: OpenAI model name. Bare family names accepted by provider=openai (e.g. gpt-5).

AnthropicModel.description: Anthropic model name. Bare family names accepted by provider=anthropic (e.g. claude-opus-4).

OpenRouterModel.description: OpenRouter model name in `provider/model` form (e.g. openai/gpt-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4.5, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, openrouter/fusion). OpenRouter-native models are now prefixed `openrouter/` (e.g. openrouter/fusion); bare forms like `fusion`, `elephant-alpha`, `hunter-alpha` no longer exist. Accepted by provider=openrouter. Reconciled against the live OpenRouter /api/v1/models catalog.

OpenRouterFreeModel.description: OpenRouter model name in `provider/model:free` form (zero-cost tier on OpenRouter). Sourced from the OpenRouter free-models collection (openrouter.ai/collections/free-models). The `:free` suffix is OpenRouter's convention for free-tier inference; callers can use this enum to expose a "free models" dropdown alongside the paid OpenRouterModel enum, or to enforce free-only policy in CI / sandboxes. Accepted by provider=openrouter.
